h: Milah and Shabbos Begin the Repair of Selfish Pleasure

p: In these parshiyos there are mentioned
the impurity of childbirth, tzaraas, and the zavah.
And in the parshah of nega'im and of the zavah it says:
וַיְדַבֵּר ה׳ אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן
"And Hashem spoke to Moshe and to Aharon";
while in the parshah of childbirth it is written:
The metzora is sent out of all three camps,
for he corresponds to the kelipah of anger,
which has no share at all in Yisrael;
while the zav is sent out only from the camp of the Levites,
for he corresponds to the kelipah of desire;
דְּלָזֶה אֵין עֵצָה רַק תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה
for which there is no counsel but the study of Torah,
that is, that he bring the yetzer and the desire
to become the longing for Torah,
as it was created for this purpose,
and as it will be in the future
(כִּדְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם חֵלֶק א קלח, א)
(as stated in Midrash HaNe'elam, Zohar I 138a);
and as they said in the Gemara (Sukkah 52b):
drag him to the beis midrash," etc.
he is sent out only from the camp of the Levites,
"They shall teach Your judgments to Yaakov
"And you shall come to the kohanim the Levites, etc."
And here it begins with the impurity of childbirth:
וְטָמְאָה שִׁבְעַת יָמִים וְגוֹ׳ (וַיִּקְרָא יב, ב)
"And she shall be impure seven days, etc." (Vayikra 12:2),
"and on the eighth day shall be circumcised, etc." (12:3).
the connection of the mitzvah of milah to here.
that "whoever's mother is not impure with childbirth
is not circumcised on the eighth day,"
But according to the view that he is circumcised on the eighth,
what is the connection of the mitzvah of milah
And the halachah was not clarified either
(as written in the Rif and the Rosh;
וּבְיוֹרֶה דֵּעָה סִימָן רסב סְעִיף ג
and in Yoreh De'ah siman 262, se'if 3
it rules that he is circumcised on the eighth).
But the matter of the impurity of childbirth,
which applies even to a "dry birth,"
and even if she gives birth to a tzaddik,
and even when Mashiach is born,
may it be speedily in our days,
nevertheless his mother is impure with childbirth
so what is the reason for this impurity?
אַךְ הִיא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
But it is based on what they said
in Midrash Rabbah (on this parshah, Vayikra Rabbah 14):
"'Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity' (Tehillim 51:7)
(according to the reading of the Aruch, entry Ayin):
Even the most pious of the pious, etc.:
And this is said about Yishai,
who died through the counsel of the serpent,
and the counsel of the serpent
is what the serpent introduced into man,
that he feel his own pleasure.
And from this sprouted the impurity of niddah,
these are the two drops of blood, etc.;
וּמִזֶּה נִצְמַח טֻמְאַת לֵידָה כָּל ז׳
and from this sprouted the impurity of childbirth all seven days.
"And on the eighth day shall be circumcised, etc.";
and then the blood of purity begins,
and even though she sees blood she is pure,
for from then she has borne a tzaddik;
for whoever is circumcised is called a tzaddik
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב כג, א)
And this is what is written in the holy Zohar
this is the blood of milah";
and nevertheless, to enter the Mikdash
וְזֶה טַעַם שֶׁנִּזְכַּר מִצְוַת מִילָה כָּאן
And this is the reason the mitzvah of milah is mentioned here.
"Moshe is the groomsman of the King,
Aharon is the groomsman of the Queen, etc.;
and therefore he stands to purify
so that no impure one be found, etc."
And therefore the parshah of nega'im was said
for the whole essence of the impurity of nega'im
for he says "impure" and it is impure,
וְכֵן טָהֳרַת מְצוֹרָע עַל יְדֵי כֹּהֵן
and likewise the purification of the metzora is through a kohen;
and as is written in the holy Zohar (III 49b):
and in another place simply 'the kohen'
and that is HaKadosh Baruch Hu."
That is, the kohanim are the agents of the Merciful One
that no impure one be found;
which is not so with the impurity of childbirth,
for this comes from the counsel of the serpent,
and this will be rectified only in the future.
And likewise at the receiving of the Torah,
for then, had there not been the corruption,
the entire corruption of the serpent would have been rectified,
for there would have been no death
And therefore the parshah of the woman giving birth was said
for he brought the Torah down to the earth
to rectify the corruption of the serpent.
And Shabbos is a semblance of Olam HaBa,
and it is the time to rectify
the first corruption of the serpent,
which was to bring into man
and on Shabbos even his own pleasure
is in holiness, as has been said.
